title: ICE Detainee Edwin Lopez-Cornejo Dies at Delaney Hall; Third Death at Facility
excerpt: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old Salvadoran man detained at Delaney Hall in Newark, N.J., died at University Hospital on August 1, 2026 after suffering a medical emergency in custody. He became the third person known to have died after a medical emergency at Delaney Hall, a facility investigators had previously found to have contaminated food, extreme temperatures, and overcrowding.
content:
Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old citizen of El Salvador, died on August 1, 2026, at University Hospital in Newark, New Jersey, after experiencing a medical emergency while detained at the Delaney Hall detention facility operated by GEO Group.

Lopez-Cornejo was the third person known to have died after experiencing a medical emergency at Delaney Hall. A prior investigation of the facility found contaminated food, extreme temperatures, overcrowding, and one detainee with an active case of tuberculosis. State health inspectors had been repeatedly denied entry to the facility.

  • DHS confirmed the death and said Lopez-Cornejo "received proper medical care" during his detention, a characterization his family disputed.
  • His sister told CNN he was being held in a crowded cell with about 10 detainees who shared one open toilet.
  • A few weeks before Lopez-Cornejo's death, another man at Delaney Hall died after suffering a seizure—he had been granted a "discretionary release" and later died at the same hospital.
  • As of August 4, 2026, NIPNLG reported at least 24 people had died in ICE custody in 2026 alone, with deaths on pace to break the 2025 record of 33—itself the highest total in more than two decades.
"More people detained means more people will die. At this pace we can expect the 2026 death toll to break last year's record." — National Immigration Project
